findings.summary:
D897 stores `— ` where the page does not read a dialogue line. keepDialogue’s test is a byte pattern, `preg_match('/^--\x20\S/', $text)`, so its `\S` takes the lead byte of a Unicode space typed after `-- ` (U+00A0, U+2009, U+202F, U+3000); the page’s dialogue dash, `/^(?:--|—)\x20(?=\S)/u`, refuses the same line. With Fine typography and fix on save, `

-- ⍽So it was.

` (⍽ = a raw U+00A0) is stored `

— ⍽So it was.

` and the page shows it so, where the same text never stored shows `

– ⍽So it was.

` (en-US, en-GB and fr alike). At 7ee012f storage kept the typed `-- ` there and page(stored) equalled page(typed). It breaks the invariant the engine-service F6 check names (“the dialogue dash, as for text never stored”) and README:120 (“the page sets it as dialogue, as it does a typed `-- `”). 99 of the 85,808 stored rows D897 changes in the differential; body text (`

`) included.

notBlocking.summary:
A French heading that ends in a mark set with U+202F (`?`, `!`, `:`, `;`, `»`) gets no widow control: the last space widows find is the narrow one, which the new guard leaves, so the two words before it are never joined (`

` → `Il a dit quoi⁔?`; the last line can be `quoi ?`). README:62 promises “a no-break space between the last two words of a heading”. Not a regression: 7ee012f gave the same on pass 1 and on pass 2 swapped the U+202F for U+00A0, which is worse; the guard makes the gap stable rather than flapping.
